correctness.rationale: For characteristic-zero K and d≥3, equality of weighted Hilbert functions of (x²,y^d) and (x^d,y²) forces weight u=v; opposite lex degree-two terms force f=Ax²+Bxy+Cy² with A,C≠0. Pure last-degree initial generators and colength give I=(f,x^d), y^d∈I. Degree-d quotient identifies with K[t]/(A+Bt+Ct²), and t^d scalar implies distinct nonzero roots α,β in characteristic zero with (α/β)^d=1 and trace ζ+ζ⁻¹∈K. Conversely g=t²−(ζ+ζ⁻¹)t+1 (ζ≠−1), or t²−1, constructs the edge. Rational traces yield orders 2,3,4,6, so rational iff 2|d or 3|d; real traces exist for all d. For odd d the smallest prime p|d minimizes φ(m)/2 to (p−1)/2 and Q(ζ_p+ζ_p⁻¹) attains it. Traces are exact, not numerical. The standard-library checker was read: finite cases do not establish universal statement.
